findings.title: f64 export claim is false; f32 arrays reach the wire encoder
findings.description:
The design says `export_positions()` / `export_velocities()` "return f64 arrays (Quadrants upcasts on download)", so the `TickResult` "carries f64". The code says otherwise:
- `src/migratory/bench/backends/quadrants_fused_state.py:242` and `:253` cast to `np.float32` explicitly.
- `tests/bench/test_quadrants_fused.py:142,145` pin `float32`.
- `TickResult.from_quadrants_fields` passes f32 through unchanged (`src/migratory/engine/tick_result.py:145-154`).

Downstream, `serialize_state_update` / `serialize_snapshot` call `.tobytes()` with no cast (`src/migratory_server/protocol.py:185-187, 210-213`), and the decoder reads `<f8`. The GPU path would therefore emit half-size payloads to clients and the sim log. A3 ("zero changes downstream") is unmet. The design must name where the f64 cast happens; changing the export methods would break the pinned bench tests and A5.

findings.title: EntityManager state is never updated on the GPU path
findings.description:
The CPU `tick()` mutates `entity_manager.state` in place (`src/migratory/engine/tick.py:117-132`). The GPU driver returns fresh arrays and never writes back, so `entity_manager.state` stays at spawn values. Consumers the design does not account for:
- `make_snapshot_builder` builds every new client's SNAPSHOT from `em.state` (`src/migratory_server/clients.py:361`), so late joiners get tick-0 positions.
- `EntityManager.get_position` (`src/migratory_server/entities.py:206-215`) returns stale data.
- `sync_from_entity_manager()` (slice line 89-90) re-uploads this stale state, so any spawn or despawn would reset every agent to its spawn position.

The lightest fix is to copy the downloaded arrays into `entity_manager.state` each tick and return `TickResult.from_numpy_state`; that also resolves the f64 finding above.

findings.title: Spawn/despawn sync cannot work as specified
findings.description:
Four defects in the sequence the slice plan assigns to this slice:
- **Fixed field extent.** Fields are placed at extent `n` once (`quadrants_fused_state.py:179-197`). "Re-upload via `from_numpy()`" with a different count is a shape mismatch. The design names neither capacity-sized allocation nor a rebuild, and a rebuild means a second `qd.init`, which line 382 calls undefined behaviour.
- **Count equality misses changes.** One spawn plus one remove leaves the count unchanged, while `remove_entity` shifts indices (`entities.py:184-200`).
- **Wrong owner.** `count_changed_since_last_tick()` is specified relative to "the previous `step()` call", which `EntityManager` knows nothing about. It also needs defined behaviour on the first tick.
- **Stale pending array.** After a count change, `sync_from_entity_manager()` runs, then `driver.step()` sees `_positions_dirty` and uploads the old-length `_pending_positions` (line 213). Nothing clears the flag on sync.

findings.title: GPU path ignores the force list; soft bounds and predator–prey forces vanish
findings.description:
The fused kernel computes cohesion, alignment, separation, leadership, momentum and propulsion only (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:186-395`). `build_forces` also produces `FlightForce` / `PursuitForce` for `interactions` and `WorldBoundsRepulsor` for `policy: soft` (`src/migratory_server/force_builder.py:64-78`). The dispatch at lines 177-183 bypasses `self._forces`.

- With `quadrants` as default, any config with `interactions` or `policy: soft` silently loses those behaviours.
- "REFLECT and SOFT: same sync-back pattern" is wrong for SOFT: `apply_bounds_policy` is a no-op there (`bounds_enforcement.py:41-42`). SOFT on GPU behaves as OPEN, so A4 cannot hold.
- Line 213 then uploads unmodified positions every tick under SOFT.

The design must reject, fall back to CPU with a warning, or implement these forces.

findings.title: Reflect sync-back uploads positions only
findings.description: `_apply_reflect` flips velocities as well as clamping positions (`bounds_enforcement.py:76-91`). `notify_positions_modified(positions)` and `upload_positions()` carry positions only, so the GPU keeps the outward velocity. Agents get pushed out and re-clamped every tick, and the velocities broadcast to clients disagree with the GPU's. Reflect needs a velocity upload too.

findings.title: `_select_arch()` detects platform, not GPU; A7 is unmet and contradicts Open Notes
findings.description:
The function returns `qd.cuda` for every Linux host and `qd.metal` for every Darwin host. The `qd.cpu` branch is reachable only on other OSes. A Linux host without CUDA never takes the warn-and-fallback path that A7 (line 336) and the slice plan entry (plan line 44) require.

Line 382 says the opposite of A7: "If `qd.init()` raises (e.g. CUDA driver absent) … the server exits". If Quadrants instead falls back internally, there is no WARNING from this code and `gpu_driver.arch` logs the wrong arch. The design needs try-init-then-fallback (or a capability probe) and must report the arch actually initialised.

findings.title: Defaulting to `quadrants` breaks existing in-process server tests and zero-entity startup
findings.description:
Existing tests build `SimulationConfig` directly and run `Server.run()` in-process dozens of times: `tests/test_server.py`, `tests/test_integration_terrain_v2.py`, `tests/test_logging_sim.py:558`, `tests/load/conftest.py:113-114`. With the new default each would construct a driver.

- **Empty configs.** Many use `profiles=[]`, `populations=[]` (`tests/test_server.py:59-60`), as does `config/no-populations.yaml`. `setup_from_server` then needs `max(query_radius)` over no profiles and a zero-extent field; the existing setup logic raises there (`quadrants_fused_state.py:140, 179`). `step()` guards `count > 0`, but `setup()` runs unconditionally at startup (lines 235-243).
- **Repeated init.** Populated configs (`tests/test_server.py:220-230`) would call `qd.init` repeatedly in one pytest process. That process already holds `ti.init(arch=ti.cpu)` from `tests/spatial/*`, `tests/forces/conftest.py:92` and `tests/bench/test_quadrants_kernels.py:35`. Line 382 calls this undefined behaviour.
- **No-CUDA Linux CI** fails outright, per the arch finding above.

The design names no handling: no test default, no skip-when-empty rule, no fixture change.

findings.title: Moving `GpuAgentState` creates a circular import and leaves the production→bench dependency
findings.description:
Line 383 claims the move "eliminates the production→bench import dependency". It does not:
- `GpuAgentState.setup(workload)` stays "unchanged" (line 152) and imports `_build_initial_state` and `Workload` from bench (`quadrants_fused_state.py:25-26`).
- The driver's `build_spatial_hash` and `fused_force_integrate_kernel` live in `bench/backends/quadrants_fused_kernels.py`, which Files Changed does not move. Importing them runs `bench/backends/__init__.py:61-65`, registering every bench backend inside the server.
- If the server imports `migratory.gpu.agent_state` first, that module imports `migratory.bench.backends.numpy_backend`. The package `__init__` then imports `quadrants_fused_backend`, which imports the still-initialising `migratory.gpu.agent_state`, giving an ImportError at startup.

Unlisted importers of the old path: `quadrants_fused_kernels.py:33`, `tests/bench/test_quadrants_fused.py:96,167,318`, `tests/bench/test_quadrants_fused_kernels.py:78,153`, `scripts/148_measure_cell_occupancy.py:28`. Without a re-export shim, A5 ("pass without modification") fails. The kernels must move too, and `setup(workload)` must lose its module-level bench imports.

findings.title: `setup_from_server()` makes the engine package depend on server types
findings.description: `src/migratory/gpu/agent_state.py` would take `EntityManager` and `WorldBoundsConfig` from `migratory_server`. Nothing in `src/migratory` imports `migratory_server` today. Take plain values instead (arrays, `world_w`, `world_h`, `dt`, `subdivision_factor`) and let `GpuSimulationDriver` unpack the server types.

findings.title: Scope and Files Changed contradict each other on the bench harness
findings.description:
- Line 296 changes `quadrants_fused_backend.py`; line 301 says it is "not changed"; line 40 puts any bench change out of scope.
- Line 34 says `_select_arch()` is "updated"; line 98 says "updated from the bench backend version". It is unclear whether the bench function at `quadrants_fused_backend.py:46-62` is modified or copied. Modifying it reverses the documented "raises explicitly with no silent CPU fallback" behaviour (`CHANGELOG.md:35`) and lets bench runs record CPU numbers under a GPU label.

State that the driver gets its own selector and the bench one is untouched.

findings.title: Deferred dirty-flag sync-back is heavier than needed
findings.description:
`notify_positions_modified()`, `_positions_dirty`, `_pending_positions` and the next-tick upload add a public method and cross-tick state. They transfer exactly what an immediate upload after `apply_bounds_policy()` would. The deferral is also the source of the stale-array ordering bug above. Cut it for one `driver.write_back(positions, velocities)` call in the same `step()`.

Also, `step()` downloads `profile_indices` every tick (line 122) although they change only on spawn/despawn; cache it.

findings.title: Runtime GPU failure and shutdown are not specified
findings.description:
- Line 254 relies on a teardown that "calls `simulation_manager` cleanup". None exists (`src/migratory_server/server.py:618-627`), and the design does not say where `finalize()` goes relative to `_sim_executor.shutdown(wait=True)`.
- If `setup()` raises after `qd.init` (line 382 mentions OOM during field allocation), nothing calls `finalize()`.
- Line 382 calls a mid-session failure "fatal to the process" without naming the mechanism. `driver.step()` runs in an executor between `barrier.begin_tick()` and `barrier.end_tick()` (`server.py:580-583`); an exception there skips `end_tick()`.
- A hung kernel or sync has no timeout or handling.

findings.title: Thread affinity of the Quadrants runtime is unstated
findings.description: `setup()` (and `qd.init`) run on the event-loop thread, `step()` runs on the single-worker `sim` executor thread (`server.py:456-458, 582`), and `finalize()` runs on the loop thread again. I did not verify whether Quadrants tolerates this. The design should either say it does or initialise on the sim executor.

findings.title: Config validation raises `ValueError`, but the entry point catches only `ConfigError`
findings.description: Every existing validator raises `ConfigError`, and `__main__.py:49-51` catches only that. A `ValueError` for `backend: turbofish` (tests 3–4, line 356) surfaces as a traceback rather than "Configuration error: …" with exit code 1. Use `ConfigError`, add a `_validate_compute` in the style of `_validate_spatial`, and specify non-int and bool handling for `subdivision_factor`.

findings.title: Verification walkthrough cannot run as written
findings.description:
- Line 348 passes the config as a positional argument; the CLI accepts only `--config` (`__main__.py:19-27`), so argparse rejects it.
- Line 351 says "Restore `backend: cpu`", but `quadrants` was the starting state.
- Lines 358-362 ("CPU default") say removing the `compute:` block selects CPU. The default is `quadrants` (line 61, A1).
- Line 362 identifies the CPU path by the spatial-backend log line. `server.py:526` logs that line on both paths.
- Line 342 edits `default.yaml`, while Files Changed (line 298) already adds a commented block there.

findings.title: Test plan is misplaced, contradictory and under-specified on isolation
findings.description:
- `tests/server/` does not exist; server tests are flat (`tests/test_server.py`, `tests/test_simulation.py`, `tests/test_config.py`). The regression command at line 375 therefore runs none of them, although those are the tests this slice puts at risk.
- Line 307 says "All tests are CPU-only", then describes running on Metal/CUDA with no mock.
- "Skip if `quadrants` not importable" is moot: it is a hard dependency (`pyproject.toml:15`).
- Config-parse tests 1–4 would be skipped on GPU-less hosts for no reason; they belong in `tests/test_config.py`.
- Tests 5–8 each call `setup()`. Line 382 leaves isolation as "either/or"; the existing convention is one subprocess per test (`tests/bench/test_quadrants_fused.py:6-16`).
- Test 6 asserts a method "is called" with no mock.
- No test covers A4 for reflect or soft, A7, or the dtype of the returned `TickResult`.

findings.title: Tier 2 gate test omits the parameters that decide the result
findings.description:
The 60 TPS at N=50k target is restated, but the test does not fix:
- `subdivision_factor`: the default is 1, while the existing gate uses S=3 (`tests/load/test_quadrants_fused_tps.py:1-7`), and the plan records 38 TPS at 50k before slices 148/149 (plan line 48).
- World size and density.
- Bounds policy: `wrap`, the `default.yaml` policy, adds the per-tick upload.
- Warm-up ticks: the first ticks include kernel compilation.
- Subprocess isolation.

Line 384's "~200 KB" covers one f32 axis; positions are two.

findings.title: References to existing code are wrong
findings.description:
- `src/migratory_server/entity_manager.py` does not exist; the class is in `entities.py`.
- `_build_forces()` (line 231) is `build_forces` from `force_builder.py`, called at `server.py:502`.
- The startup snippet uses `config.…`, `entity_manager`, `profile_list`; the code has `self.config`, `self.entity_manager`, `self.entity_manager.profile_list`.
- Line 119 says "three phases" and lists four.
- `arch` is `"metal" | "cuda" | "cpu"` at line 224 but `"cuda"` or `"metal"` at line 252.
- The `step()` listing (lines 171-199) omits the `notify_positions_modified` call that line 213 requires.

findings.title: CPU-path setup still runs under `quadrants`
findings.description: `_warm_force_kernels()` (2–4 s of Numba compile, `server.py:515`) and `_build_spatial()` still execute, and `simulation.spatial` becomes silently inert. A logged line saying so would be enough; skipping the warm-up is optional.

findings.title: Plan's f64-on-CUDA direction differs from the shipped f32 kernels
findings.description: Plan lines 36 and 40 describe slice 145 as f64 throughout on CUDA. The shipped kernels are f32 (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py:223`). The design correctly follows the code; the plan text is stale.

findings.title: Config surface, driver ownership and call-site shape match the slice plan entry
findings.description: `simulation.compute` with `backend: quadrants | cpu` and `subdivision_factor`, default `quadrants`, a `GpuSimulationDriver` owning the `qd.init` / `GpuAgentState` lifecycle, and dispatch inside `SimulationManager.step()` all match plan line 44. The `[1, 8]` range matches `_SUBDIVISION_FACTOR_MIN/MAX` (`quadrants_fused_state.py:52-53`). The optional `gpu_driver=None` parameter leaves existing `SimulationManager(...)` callers unaffected. Dependency (145) and effort 3 match.

findings.title: Tier 2 NFR is restated with its target
findings.description: A6 restates ≥60 TPS at N=50k on CUDA from plan line 74.
